draft.title: Dimensions of health
card: Health is more than not being sick. It has five dimensions, and each one is part of overall wellbeing.
Physical
how well the body works, such as fitness, energy and strength. Mental: how a person thinks, learns and makes decisions.
Emotional and social
Emotional is how a person recognises and manages feelings. Social is the quality of relationships and connection to others, such as friends, family and teams.
Spiritual
a sense of meaning, purpose and values, which may come from beliefs, culture, faith or connection to nature. The five dimensions affect each other, so a change in one can lead to changes in another.
draft.remember: Health has five dimensions, and what happens in one can affect the others.

a.q: Which example shows the social dimension of health?
opts: Having close friends to talk to and spend time with
Being able to run 5 km without stopping
Feeling calm after a stressful exam
Feeling that life has meaning and purpose
a.why: The social dimension is about relationships and connection with others, so having close friends fits. Running 5 km is physical, feeling calm is emotional, and a sense of purpose is spiritual.
a.clue: Which one is about connection with other people?

b.q: Jas breaks his leg and cannot play in his football team for three months. He stops seeing his teammates and feels low. Which statement best describes what is happening?
opts: An injury to his body is also changing his social and emotional health
Only his physical health is affected, because the injury is to his leg
His low mood caused the broken leg, so the dimensions work in reverse
His social health is affected, but his emotions stay unchanged by it
b.why: The injury is physical, but losing contact with teammates affects his social health and feeling low affects his emotional health. The dimensions affect each other, so saying only the physical dimension is affected is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what else changed for Jas besides his leg.
